findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default KeyStore's provider instead of a BouncyCastle provider
findings.description: The method is named and typed as the BouncyCastle provider accessor, but its body returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`. That is the JDK keystore's provider, not a BouncyCastle provider. Callers that expect a BC provider (for example, a lookup by name) will receive an unrelated provider. The other providers in this diff (`DefaultCryptoProvider`, `FIPS1402Provider`) return a real BC instance from this method.

findings.title: concatenatedRSToASN1DER builds two encoders and discards them
findings.description: The two statements `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` have no effect because their results are not used. The return value is built correctly by the subsequent `writeDerSeq(...)` call, so these lines are dead code and can be removed.

findings.title: getKeyStore uses format.name() while the FIPS provider uses format.toString()
findings.description: `AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getKeyStore` calls `KeyStore.getInstance(format.name())`, while `FIPS1402Provider.getKeyStore` calls `format.toString()`. Both produce the same result only if `KeystoreFormat.toString()` is not overridden. This should be checked against the enum definition.

findings.title: Ignored-provider log passes a built string as the format argument, and leaves a trailing separator
findings.description: `logger.debugf(builder.toString())` uses a non-literal string as the format pattern. Any `%` in a provider class name would be interpreted as a format specifier. The loop also appends `", "` after every name, leaving a trailing separator. Passing the format as a literal with a `%s` argument, and joining the names without a trailing separator, would fix both.
